response.rationale: Negative HSV, fungal, bacterial, and complement studies make herpetic, fungal, bacterial, and angioedema diagnoses unlikely. In an HIV patient with recovered CD4 count and painful proliferative/ulcerated oral lesions, Kaposi sarcoma is most consistent, commonly occurring in the setting of immune reconstitution; IRIS alone does not specify the lesion.

rejected.why: Herpes simplex was contradicted by a negative PCR assay.
Fungal infection was contradicted by negative fungal cultures, Histoplasma antigen, and mucicarmine stain.
Herpetic ulcers have the same negative HSV PCR contradiction.
Bacillary angiomatosis lacks supporting histologic or confirmatory evidence and the lesions did not respond to antibiotic courses.
Angioedema was contradicted by a normal C1 esterase inhibitor level.
IRIS is only the immune mechanism, while Kaposi sarcoma better specifies the clinical diagnosis.
